Useful strings from the packet format

Start
 │
 ├── Does input begin with PKT1;?
 │      ├── No  → rejected
 │      └── Yes → continue
 │
 ├── What is TYPE?
 │      ├── TEXT   → TEXT branch
 │      ├── NUMBER → NUMBER branch
 │      ├── META   → META branch
 │      └── Other  → rejected
 │
 └── What is ACTION?
        ├── SHOW
        ├── COUNT
        ├── STORE
        └── Other → rejected

TYPE=TEXT
    ↓
enter the TEXT branch
    ↓
continue to ACTION

TYPE=NUMBER
    ↓
call observe_number(DATA)
    ↓
continue to ACTION

DATA missing or empty  → stop numeric processing
DATA contains letters  → stop numeric processing
DATA is 165            → special 165 branch
DATA is greater than 1000 → large-number branch
Other number           → ordinary number path

TYPE=META
    ↓
Does DATA begin with CS165?
    ├── Yes → special CS165 branch
    └── No  → ordinary META branch
    ↓
continue to ACTION

ACTION=SHOW
    ↓
Does DATA exist?
    ├── Yes → accepted
    └── No  → rejected

TEXT + SHOW
NUMBER + SHOW
META + SHOW

ACTION=COUNT
    ↓
Does DATA exist?
    ├── Yes → accepted
    └── No  → rejected

TEXT + COUNT
NUMBER + COUNT
META + COUNT

ACTION=STORE
    ↓
Is AUTH=YES?
    ├── No  → rejected
    └── Yes
          ↓
Is TYPE=TEXT?
    ├── No  → rejected
    └── Yes
          ↓
Does DATA exist?
    ├── No  → rejected
    └── Yes
          ↓
Allocate 16 bytes
          ↓
Was allocation successful?
    ├── No  → rejected
    └── Yes
          ↓
Copy DATA

DATA length ≤ 16
    → safe copy
    → accepted

DATA length > 16
    → heap-buffer-overflow
    → AddressSanitizer reports a crash

title: Blind mutation and coverage guided mutation

elements.text: Blind mutation and coverage guided mutation
Mutates a seed and only notices a crash or timeout. It does not know whether an input reached a new branch.
Measures execution coverage and keeps inputs that add new behavior. Useful discoveries become future mutation targets.
Both use mutation. Coverage feedback changes the search strategy.
Structured formats often contain multi-byte words that random byte changes rarely assemble.
tokens.dict supplies packet fragments to the mutation engine.

The dictionary does not define the full grammar
The fuzzer still decides where to insert tokens
Coverage still decides which results are useful
A memory bug may silently corrupt data during a normal run. AddressSanitizer adds checks that stop the program and report the violation.
The STORE path allocates 16 bytes but copies payload.len bytes.
heap-buffer-overflow with a stack trace and source location.
libFuzzer writes the triggering bytes to a crash-* file.
The sanitizer finds the memory violation. The fuzzer finds an input that reaches it.
A new useful input entered the corpus
A smaller input kept existing behavior
Campaigns are stochastic. Output and execution counts vary.
Run the same binary with that file
Check the sanitizer class and source location
Remove bytes while preserving the failure
A minimized input makes the root cause easier to understand and easier to test later.

Question: what is the smallest input that still causes this failure?

Output: one compact crash trigger.

Question: what is the smallest set of inputs that preserves the corpus coverage?

Output: a smaller set of useful inputs.
